questions.question: What is the purpose of an Organization alias?
options: It replaces the Organization ID on invoices
It is an easier-to-remember alternative to the Organization ID for Member login
It is a prefix added to every Project name
It is the username of the Organization Owner
questions.topic: Manage Your Organization & Projects
questions.explanation: An alias identifies the Organization during Member login, as an alternative to the Organization ID.

questions.question: When an Organization Owner leaves, how is ownership transferred?
options: Promote a Member to Owner with an IAM policy
Add a second Owner to the Organization
Change the email address registered on the Owner account
Create a new Organization and move all Projects into it
questions.topic: Manage Your Organization & Projects
questions.explanation: An Organization has a single Owner and a Member cannot be promoted to Owner; ownership is transferred by changing the email address of the Owner account.

questions.question: Which two statements about deleting a Project are true?
options: A Project can only be deleted once all its resources are deleted
Deleting a Project moves its resources to the default Project
The default Project cannot be deleted
Only Scaleway Support can delete a Project
questions.topic: Manage Your Organization & Projects
questions.explanation: Only empty Projects can be deleted, and the default Project cannot be deleted.

questions.question: Which two features are managed at the Organization level rather than Project level?
questions.topic: Manage Your Organization & Projects
questions.explanation: Billing, IAM, support and abuse tickets and Project management are managed at Organization level, while resources such as Instances and buckets belong to Projects.

questions.question: Which two benefits does grouping resources into separate Projects provide?
options: Resources can be moved freely between Projects at any time
IAM access rights can be defined separately per Project
Resource usage is easier to track on invoices
Each Project has its own Owner account
questions.topic: Manage Your Organization & Projects
questions.explanation: Grouping resources into Projects lets you define custom IAM access rights per Project and makes it easier to track resource usage on your invoices.

questions.question: At what granularity do Organization quotas apply?
options: Per product and product type, e.g., an Instance type
As a single total number of resources for the whole Organization
questions.topic: Manage Your Organization & Projects
questions.explanation: Quotas are limits on the number of resources an Organization can use, and they apply per product and product type.

questions.question: Where can Organization quotas be viewed in the Scaleway console?
options: In the Policies tab of the IAM dashboard
In the Invoices tab of the Billing section
In the Quotas tab of the Organization dashboard
In the Data sources tab of Cockpit
questions.topic: Manage Your Organization & Projects
questions.explanation: Organization quotas are listed in the Quotas tab of the Organization dashboard, where they can be filtered by product and location.

questions.question: Which CLI command creates a Project?
questions.topic: Manage Your Organization & Projects
questions.explanation: Projects are managed with the scw account project commands (create, get, list, update, delete).

questions.question: What is automatically created when you create a Scaleway account?
options: An Owner-led Organization with a default Project
An IAM application with a full-access API key
questions.topic: Manage Your Organization & Projects
questions.explanation: An Organization is created automatically with you as Owner, and each Organization comes with a default Project.

questions.question: What does an IAM rule consist of?
options: A principal and an API key
A scope with one or more permission sets
A Project and a secret key
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: A rule is made of a scope (Project or Organization level) and one or more permission sets, with optional conditions.

questions.question: Can an IAM rule explicitly deny access to specific actions or resources?
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: Rules can only give access; the default for anyone other than the Owner is zero permissions beyond those granted by attached policies.

questions.question: A newly created IAM Member has no policy attached. What can they do?
options: Nothing beyond what attached policies grant
Read all resources but not modify them
Access resources of the default Project only
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: Apart from the Owner, a user starts with zero permissions other than those defined by the policies attached to them.

questions.question: Policy A allows app access Mondays only; Policy B with same principal allows Tuesdays only. When is access possible?
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: IAM policies have no priority and do not compete: a single policy with met conditions allows the action, so access is granted on both days.

questions.question: Which two attributes can an IAM request-level condition evaluate?
options: The IP address of the request
The CPU load of the targeted Instance
The MFA status of the caller
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: Request-level conditions are written in CEL and use the request IP address, user agent and time.

questions.question: Which statement about API key generation is accurate?
options: An Owner can create keys for any IAM user
You can create keys for your own user, not other human users
API keys only for IAM applications
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: API keys can be generated for your own user or for an IAM application, but not for other human IAM users, whatever your permissions.

questions.question: After setting max API key duration at Organization level, what happens to existing keys?
options: Their expiration is shortened to the new maximum
They are not affected; applies to new keys only
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: Setting or changing the maximum duration does not retroactively affect existing API keys, and the expiration date of an existing key cannot be modified.

questions.question: Which two measures help limit the impact of a leaked API key?
options: Share a single API key among all team members
Enforce maximum duration for API keys
Store secret key in the source repository
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: Limiting credential lifetime reduces the risk of leaked credentials remaining valid, and rotating keys is a documented good practice.

questions.question: MFA enforced in Organization, Member hasn't enabled it when grace period ends. What happens?
options: MFA is disabled for that Member
Member's account is locked until unlocked by Owner
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: Members who do not comply with the enforced security requirements before the grace period ends are automatically locked and must be manually unlocked.

questions.question: When a Member is locked, do their API keys keep their permissions?
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: API keys attached to a Member lose their permissions when the Member is locked.

questions.question: What does Scaleway create automatically in IAM when you create a Kubernetes Kapsule cluster?
options: An IAM group containing cluster nodes as applications, with a policy attached
A new Organization dedicated to the cluster
An API key for each Project user
A policy granting AllProductsFullAccess to the cluster creator
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: Creating a cluster generates a group of node applications and a default policy with that group as principal, which can be deleted but not edited.

questions.question: You want a user and application to receive identical permissions through one policy. What should you do?
options: Attach the policy to both separately
Give the application the user's API key
Add both to an IAM group and attach the policy
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: A policy can be attached to only one principal, so a group lets one policy apply to several users and applications.

questions.question: Which CLI command creates an API key for an IAM application?
questions.topic: Manage access to your Organization's resources
questions.explanation: scw iam api-key create takes an application-id or a user-id, and an optional default-project-id for Object Storage.

questions.question: A secret in Secret Manager must hold a new database password. How do you store the new value?
options: Move the secret to another region
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: A secret is a logical container of immutable versions, so a new value is stored by adding a version.

questions.question: What happens when you delete a secret from the Scaleway console?
options: Scheduled deletion with a pending period
Only the latest version is deleted
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: Deleting a secret schedules its deletion, with a pending period during which it can be recovered before permanent deletion.

questions.question: Which two actions can an ephemeral policy apply to an expired secret version?
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: An ephemeral policy lets you choose whether expired versions are disabled or deleted.

questions.question: In Scaleway's External Secrets tutorial on Kapsule, what does an External Secret do?
options: It creates a Kubernetes Secret from a Scaleway secret
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: An ExternalSecret specifies which secret to fetch from Secret Manager, and External Secrets creates a Kubernetes Secret containing it, whereas the Secret Manager CSI provider mounts secrets into pods without creating Kubernetes Secrets.

questions.question: Which CLI command returns the value of a secret version?
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: scw secret version access returns the sensitive data of a version, whereas scw secret secret get returns only metadata.

questions.question: In the Scaleway Go SDK, which Secret Manager API method returns the value of a secret version?
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: The secret package of the Scaleway Go SDK exposes AccessSecretVersion and AccessSecretVersionByPath to read version data.

questions.question: A dedicated application pulls secrets with External Secrets on Kapsule. Which two configurations apply?
options: Reference the secret in a Kubernetes Secret
Use an IAM policy with Secret Manager access
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: The documented minimum permission sets for an application using External Secrets are SecretManagerReadOnly and SecretManagerSecretAccess.

questions.question: Key Manager generates a data encryption key (DEK) for your application. How should you handle it?
options: Rely on Key Manager to store the DEK
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: Key Manager does not store DEKs; you should keep only their ciphertext, never store the plaintext and delete it after use.

questions.question: After rotating a symmetric Key Manager key, can previously encrypted data still be decrypted?
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: Data encrypted with former key versions remains decipherable with the former version as long as the key is not deleted.

questions.question: Which statements describe Key Manager advantages over storing encryption keys in application code?
options: Keys can be exported in plaintext
Cryptographic operations happen inside Key Manager, keys never leave
No permission separation between encrypt and decrypt
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: Key Manager keeps keys non-extractable and performs the operations itself, and it allows separate encrypt and decrypt authorizations.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using data encryption keys (DEKs) when encrypting data?
options: DEKs are stored in plaintext with the data
KEKs can be rotated without re-encrypting the data
DEKs eliminate the need for a KEK
questions.topic: Share and encrypt sensitive data
questions.explanation: Because data is encrypted by a DEK, rotating the key encryption key requires re-encrypting only the DEK and not the data.

questions.question: Which statuses can an Audit Trail event have?
questions.topic: Monitor your resources and immediately detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: An Audit Trail status is the API response to the action: Successful when the request was executed, Forbidden when permission was denied.

questions.question: Which two IAM permission sets let you use Audit Trail?
questions.topic: Monitor your resources and immediately detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Audit Trail requires the AuditTrailReadOnly or OrganizationManager permission set, scoped at Organization level.

questions.question: Where can Audit Trail events be exported for long-term retention?
questions.topic: Monitor your resources and immediately detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Audit Trail exports upload event logs to an Object Storage bucket of your choice.

questions.question: Which question is best answered with Audit Trail?
options: Who deleted a bucket and when?
What is the CPU usage of an Instance?
How much does Object Storage cost?
questions.topic: Monitor your resources and immediately detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Audit Trail records the identity of the principal, the date, the source IP address, the API method used and the status of the request.

questions.question: Can you modify thresholds of Scaleway preconfigured alerts in Cockpit?
questions.topic: Monitor your resources and immediately detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Preconfigured alerts come with default thresholds and evaluation durations that cannot be modified.

questions.question: You want to send your own application metrics to Cockpit. Which two statements apply?
options: Use the Scaleway API to push metrics
Use the Cockpit data source in Grafana
Use the Scaleway CLI to send metrics
questions.topic: Monitor your resources and immediately detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Scaleway data sources are read-only, so custom data needs a custom data source, and a token with the Push permission authenticates the sending.

questions.question: What happens when you reduce the retention period of a Cockpit data source?
options: The data source is temporarily paused
Older data is kept but marked as archived
Data older than the new period is deleted
questions.topic: Monitor your resources and immediately detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Reducing retention permanently deletes the data beyond the selected period, and the deletion is irreversible even if the retention is later increased.

questions.question: When creating alerting rules in Grafana for Cockpit, which type of rule applies?
questions.topic: Monitor your resources and immediately detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Scaleway does not support the Grafana alert manager, so alerting rules in Grafana must be data source-managed.

questions.question: Which two Cockpit elements provided by Scaleway are read-only?
questions.topic: Monitor your resources and immediately detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Scaleway data sources are read-only, and preconfigured dashboards in the Scaleway folder are always read-only.

questions.question: What does the preferred Project of an API key define?
options: The Project where the key was created
The Project context for API calls
The Project that owns the key
The Project where alerts are sent
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: S3-compatible tools cannot pass a Project ID, so the API key's preferred Project is the one used for Object Storage actions.

questions.question: Which two statements about bucket policies are true?
options: Bucket policies can grant access to IAM users
Bucket policies are always required for bucket access
Bucket policies can restrict access by IP address
Bucket policies can grant cross-account access
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: A bucket holds a single bucket policy, which a new push overwrites; with version 2023-04-17 only explicitly allowed actions are permitted, so Deny statements are useless.

questions.question: Several principals have Object Storage access through IAM. You add a bucket policy. What happens?
options: Both are evaluated, most restrictive wins
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: Once a bucket policy restricts access, every other principal that needs access must be explicitly allowed by the bucket policy.

questions.question: Organization Owner pushes a bucket policy that denies all access. What happens?
options: Access is denied to everyone including Owner
Owner retains access despite the deny
Access is denied only to new users
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: The Owner always has the right to put and delete bucket policies, even if the policy does not allow other bucket operations.

questions.question: After uploading an object with SSE-C, what does Object Storage retain?
options: A hash of the encryption key
The key ID but not the key itself
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: With SSE-C the key is deleted once the data is copied, and only its digest is saved in the object's metadata so the object can be decrypted on download.

questions.question: Which Object Storage server-side encryption method uses a key encryption key to wrap data encryption keys?
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS relies on a symmetric KEK from Key Manager associated with the bucket, while SSE-ONE uses keys managed by Scaleway and SSE-C uses customer-provided keys.

questions.question: Application has ObjectStorageFullAccess but no Key Manager access. What happens with SSE-KMS encrypted objects?
options: Can read but cannot decrypt objects
Can read and decrypt if key is in same Project
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: Object Storage permission sets alone are not sufficient for SSE-KMS buckets, and writing needs KeyManagerKeyEncrypt.

questions.question: Enabling SSE-ONE on an existing bucket also encrypts objects already stored?
options: Yes, after a manual re-encryption job
Only if Object Lock is enabled
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: Objects uploaded before SSE-ONE was enabled are not encrypted; only new uploads are.

questions.question: A bucket policy must allow a principal to list a bucket and read objects. Which two statements apply?
options: Allow s3:GetObject on objects with a specific prefix
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: s3:ListBucket requires the bucket resource and s3:GetObject requires <BUCKET_NAME>/*, which grants access to the objects but not to the bucket itself.

questions.question: An API key has bucket A's Project as preferred Project. How can it access bucket B in another Project?
options: It cannot, API keys are locked to one Project
Use the API key with a different Project header
Append @<Project ID> to the access key, subject to permissions on that Project
Create a new API key for bucket B's Project
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: Appending @ and a Project ID to the access key overrides the preferred Project, provided the key has permissions on the target Project.
